57:1: The statement in the interpretation of the surah in which iron is mentioned Meaning, the Most High, by His saying: Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God, that everything below Him of His creation glorifies Him in reverence for Him, acknowledging His Lordship, and submitting to His obedience, as the Most High said: “The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is therein glorify Him. There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification.” (al-Isra’ 17:44) And His statement, And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, means: But He, may His glory be exalted, is the Exalted in His vengeance upon those who disobeyed Him and violated His command from among His creation in the heavens and the earth. The Wise in His management of their affairs and His disposition of them as He willed and loved.
57:2: And His statement, To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, God Almighty says: He has authority over the heavens and the earth and everything in them, and nothing in them is able to resist Him. He has authority over all of them and His judgment is carried out. And His statement, He gives life and causes death, means: He gives life to whatever He wills of creation by creating it however He wills, by creating from the dead sperm an animal by breathing the spirit into it after a few times in which He turns it over and other things like that, and He causes to death whatever He wills of the living after life, after it has reached its appointed time, so He annihilates it. And He is over all things competent, means, may His praise be exalted, He is over all things competent, and nothing He wills of giving life and causing death, honoring and humiliating, and other matters is impossible for Him..
57:3: God Almighty says: He is the First before everything without limit. And the Last means: The Last is after everything without end. It was said thus because He was and nothing existed besides Him. He will be after the annihilation of all things, as He, the Most High, said: Everything will perish except His Face (al-Qasas 28:88). And His statement: And the Manifest means: He is the Manifest over everything below Him. He is the High above everything, so nothing is higher than Him. And the Hidden means: He is the Hidden of all things, so nothing is closer to anything than Him, as He said: And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein (Qaf: 16). In a similar manner to what we said about that, the report came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of interpretation said the same. Mention of who said that and the report that was narrated about it: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent, it was mentioned to us that while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting among his companions, a cloud rose up against them. He said, Do you know what this is? They said, God and His Messenger know best. He said, Indeed, it is the firm, restrained wave and a protected ceiling. He said, Do you know how much is between you and it? They said, God and His Messenger know best. He said, A journey of five hundred years. He said, Do you know what is above that? They said, Likewise. He said, “Above it is another heaven, and between them is a... the Throne, and between it and the seventh heaven is like what is between two heavens.” He said, Do you know what is below you? They said, God and His Messenger know best. He said, It is the earth. He said, Do you know what is below it? They said, Likewise, it is the earth. He said, Do you know what is below it? They said, It is the same as their first statement. He said, Below it is another earth, and between them is a journey of five hundred years, until he enumerated seven earths, and between every two earths is a journey of five hundred years. Then he said, “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if one of you were let down by a rope to The other earth to descend upon God then read “He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent, and He is Knowing of all things.” And His statement, And He is All-Knowing of all things, means that God Almighty says: And He is All-Knowing of all things. Nothing is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom on earth or in heaven escapes Him, nor anything smaller than that or larger, except that it is in a clear book.
57:4: And His statement, It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, God Almighty says: It is He who created the seven heavens and the earths, and administers them and what is in them, then He established Himself on His Throne, so He rose above it and was exalted above it. And His statement, He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out of it, says the Most High, informing about His description and that nothing of His creation is hidden from Him. He knows what goes into the earth of His creation, meaning by His statement, goes in, “enters,” and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky to the earth of anything, and what ascends therein, and He is with you wherever you are, meaning, He is a witness for you, O people, wherever you are. He knows you and knows your deeds, your movements, and your resting place, and He is on His throne above His seven heavens. And God is Seeing, meaning, God is All-Seeing of your deeds that you do, of good and bad, obedience and disobedience. He is a Sight Seeer, and He is their keeper, so that He may reward the doer of good among you for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing on the Day when it is recompensed. Every soul is for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. (al-Jathiyah 45:22)
57:5: God Almighty says: He has authority over the heavens and the earth, effective over all of them and over all that is in them. His command is in them, and to God all matters return. He, the Most High, says: And to God all matters return. He, the Most High, says: And to God the fate of all His creation is, and He judges between them according to His judgment.
57:6: And His statement, He causes the night to enter the day, means by His statement, He causes the night to enter the day, that He includes whatever hours of the night are missing in the day, making them an increase in its hours. And He causes the day to enter the night, means: He includes whatever hours of the day are missing in the night, making them an increase in the hours of the night. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. We have mentioned the narration of what they said in the past in this book of ours, except that we will mention in this place what we did not mention there, God willing. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, he said: The shortness of this is in the length of this and the length of this is in the shortness of this. Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, he said: The night entering the day and the day entering the night. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, he said: The shortness of the days of winter is due to the length of its nights, and the shortness of the nights of summer is due to the length of its days. And His statement, And He is All-Knowing of that within the breasts, means: He has knowledge of the secrets in the breasts of His servants and what their souls have resolved to do of good or evil or what their souls have thought of. Nothing of that is hidden from Him.
57:7: God Almighty says: Believe in God, O people, and acknowledge His Oneness and in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believe in what he brought you from God and follow him. And spend from that over which He has made you successors. God Almighty says: And spend from that over which God has given you wealth which He has inherited from those who came before you, and He has made you their successors in it, in the cause of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding God’s statement, those who are successors therein, he said: Those who live long in it with provision. And His statement, Those of you who have believed and spent, means: Those of you, O people, who have believed in God and His Messenger and spent from what God has given them on behalf of those who came before them and provided them with money in the way of God, for them is a great reward, meaning for them is a great reward.
57:8: God Almighty says: And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in God? And what is the matter with you, O people, that you do not acknowledge the Oneness of God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, calls you to acknowledge His Oneness, and He has given you proofs of the truth of that which cut off your excuse and removed doubt from your hearts. And He has taken your covenant. It was said about me in that: And your Lord has taken your covenant from you in the loins of Adam that God is your Lord, there is no god for you other than Him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And He has taken your covenant, he said, on the back of Adam. The reciters differed in the recitation of this. The reciters of Hijaz and Iraq, other than Abu Amr, recited it as and He took your covenant with the opening of the alif from to take and the accusative of the covenant, meaning: and your Lord took your covenant. Abu Amr recited it as and He took your covenant with the damma of the alif and the nominative of the covenant, as if its agent was not named. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads is correct, even though the opening of the alif in akhdha and the nasb of mithaq is more pleasing to me in this regard, due to the large number of readers who read that way and the small number of readers who read the other way. His saying, If you are believers, means: If you want to believe in God one day, then now is the most appropriate time for you to believe, so that the arguments will continue to be presented to you through the Messenger, his notification, and his calling you to what has been established as true for you through the notifications, evidence, and covenant taken from you.
57:9: God Almighty says: God is the One who sends down to His servant Muhammad clear verses, meaning detailed ones, to bring you out from darkness into the light. God Almighty says: To bring you out, O people, from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith and from misguidance to guidance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: From darkness to light, he said: From misguidance to guidance. And His statement, And indeed, God is to you Most Kind and Most Merciful, God Almighty says: And indeed, God, by sending down to His servant what He sent down to him of clear verses to guide you and enlighten you to the right path, is most kind and merciful to you. So out of His kindness and mercy toward you, He did this.
57:10: God Almighty says: And what is the matter with you, O people, that you do not spend from what God has provided you in the way of God? And to God will return your wealth if you do not spend it during your life in the way of God. For to Him belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. And He, the Most High, only urged them with that regarding their portion, saying to them: Spend your wealth in the way of God so that it may be a reserve for you with God before you die and are no longer able to do so, and the wealth becomes an inheritance for He to whom belong the heavens and the earth. And his saying: Those of you who spent before the conquest and fought are not equal. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said that it means: Those of you who believed before the conquest of Mecca and emigrated are not equal. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought, he said: He believed and spent, meaning: He who emigrated is not like he who did not emigrate. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest, meaning those who believed. He said: Mahran told us on the authority of Sufyan, who said: He says something else. Others said that the conquest meant the conquest of Mecca and the expenditure in the jihad against the polytheists. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought. Those are greater in degree than those who spent and fought afterwards. But to all God has promised good.” He said: There were two fights, one of which was better than the other, and there were two expenditures, one of which was better than the other. The spending and fighting before the conquest the conquest of Mecca were better than the spending and fighting after that. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, before the conquest, he said: The conquest of Mecca. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abdullah bin Ayyash told me: Zaid bin Aslam said about this verse, Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest, he said: The conquest of Mecca. Others said: What is meant by the opening in this place is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Who said that? Ishaq bin Shaheen told me: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, who said: The separation between the two migrations was the conquest of Hudaybiyyah. God Almighty says: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought. The verse. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told me: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Dawud told us on the authority of `Amir regarding this verse: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest. He said: The conquest of al-Hudaybiyyah. He said: The separation between the two Umrahs was the conquest of al-Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Abdul-Wahhab told us: Dawud told us on the authority of Aamer: The separation between the two migrations was the conquest of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and the verses Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest were revealed until And God is Acquainted with what you do. They said: O Messenger of God, is it a conquest? He said: Yes, it is a great one. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us on the authority of Amer, who said: The separation between the two migrations was the conquest of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Then he recited here the verse: None of you are equal… Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Hisham ibn Sa'd told me, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata' ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah: There will soon come a people whom you will consider your deeds insignificant compared to theirs. We said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? Are they Quraysh? He said: No, but the people of Yemen are more tender-hearted and soft-hearted. We said: Are they better than us, O Messenger of God? He said: "If one of them had a mountain of gold and spent it, it would not equal the measure of one of you, or even half of it. Indeed, this is the distinction between us and the al-Nas 114:'Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest'" verse until His saying: And God is Acquainted with what you do. Ibn al-Barqi told me: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Zayd ibn Aslam told me, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Tammar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There will soon come a people whose deeds you will consider insignificant compared to theirs. We said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? The Quraysh? He said: No, they are the most tender-hearted and soft-hearted. He pointed with his hand to Yemen and said: “They are the people of Yemen. Beware, faith is from Yemen and wisdom is from Yemen.” We said: O Messenger of God, are they better than us? He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of them had a mountain of gold that he could spend, it would not reach the level of one of you or even half of it. Then he joined his fingers and extended his little finger and said: “Beware, this is the distinction between us and the al-Nas 114:‘Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought. Those are greater in degree than those who spent and fought afterwards. But to all God has promised goodness.’” The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is to say: The meaning of this is that those among you, O people, who spent in the cause of God before the conquest of Hudaybiyyah are not equal to what we mentioned from the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which we narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri on his authority, and those who fought the polytheists, between those who spent after that and fought. He left out mentioning those who spent after that and fought, sufficing with the indication of the speech that he mentioned of those who mentioned it. Those are greater in degree than those who spent after that and fought. God, the Exalted, says: These are the ones who spent in the cause of God before the conquest of Hudaybiyyah and fought the polytheists, greater in degree in Paradise with God than those who spent after that and fought. And His statement: And to both of them God has promised goodness, God Almighty says: And to all of those who spent before the conquest and fought, and to those who spent afterward and fought, God has promised Paradise for their spending in His cause and their fighting His enemies. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Of those who spent afterwards and fought - to all of them God has promised good. He said: Paradise. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And to both God has promised goodness. He said: Paradise. And His statement: And God is All-Aware of what you do. God Almighty says: God is All-Aware of what you do of spending in the way of God, fighting His enemies, and other deeds that you do. Nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for all of that on the Day of Resurrection.
57:11: God the Almighty says: Who is he who spends in the cause of God in this world, expecting reward in his spending, seeking what is with God? And that is the good loan. He says: So his Lord will multiply for him his loan, that which he lent him for his spending in His cause, and He will give him seven hundred for one. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say in his statement, Who is he who would loan God a good loan? It is like the Arabs’ saying: I have with you a loan of truth and a loan of evil, if he did good with it. And he recited a verse by Shanfara in this regard: We will reward Salaman bin Mufrij for what his hands have put forth, so he removed it. And he will have a noble reward. He says: And he will have a noble reward and recompense. By that reward, he means Paradise. We have already mentioned the narration from the people of interpretation regarding that, and there is no need to repeat it.
57:12: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement, On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light proceeding before them and on their right. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light shining before them and on their right. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, the verse. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “Among the believers are those whose light will shine from Medina to Aden, Abyan, Sana’a, and beyond that, to the point that among the believers are those whose light will shine only where their feet are.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Idris told us: I heard my father mention on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Qais bin Sakn, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: They will be given their light according to the extent of their deeds. Some of them will be given their light like a palm tree, and some of them will be given their light like a standing man. The light of them with the light of the least of them will be on his thumb, sometimes it will be extinguished and sometimes it will be kindled. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: On the Day you see the believing men and believing women, their faith and guidance proceeding before them and on their right: their books. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Their light proceeds before them and on their right, that is, their books. God says: As for he who is given his book in his right hand, as for their light, it has guided him. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion we mentioned on the authority of Ad-Dahhak. That is because if he meant by that light the well-known light, he would not have made it specific to the report of striving between the hands and the right without the left, because the light of the believers that they will be given in the Hereafter will illuminate for them everything around them. And in the specific report of God, may He be glorified, about His striving between their hands and on their right without the left, there is what indicates that He meant by it something other than the light, even though they are not devoid of light. The interpretation of the statement, since the matter is as we have described: And to both of them God has promised goodness on the Day you see the believing men and believing women running, the reward of their faith and righteous deeds before them, and in their right hands the books of their deeds flying about. By his saying strives he means he goes on, and the ba in his saying and their right hands means in. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: the ba in his saying and their right hands means on their right hands. His saying: On the Day you see is from the conjunction of promise. And His statement: Your good tidings today are gardens beneath which rivers flow. God Almighty says, Your good tidings today, O believers, which you are given good tidings of, are gardens beneath which rivers flow, so rejoice in them. His saying: They will abide therein eternally means: They will remain in Paradise, never moving from it or being transformed. His saying: That is the great attainment means: Their eternity in the gardens that he described is the great success that they were seeking after being saved from God’s punishment and entering Paradise to remain there forever.
57:13: God Almighty says: It is the great victory on the Day of the hypocrites, men and women. Today is a day of victory for those who believed in God and His Messengers: Look at us. The reciters differed in their recitation of his saying Anzuruna. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited it as Anzuruna connected, meaning: wait for us. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as Anzuruna without the alif from Anzurtu meaning: delay us. Al-Farra’ mentioned that the Arabs say Anzurni and they mean: wait for me a little while. He recited in this regard the verse of Amr ibn Kulthum: Abu Hind, do not rush us and wait for us to tell you for sure. He said: The meaning of this is: Wait a little while and we will tell you, because there is no delay here, but rather listening, like when you say to a man: Listen to me so I can tell you. In my opinion, the correct reading for this is to connect it because this is what is known in the speech of the Arabs when what is meant is we waited and there is no meaning to the delay in this situation, so it is said wait us with the opening of the alif and its hamza. His saying: We take from your light means: We seek light from your light. The flame is the torch. And His saying: It will be said, Go back and seek light. He, the Most High, says: They will be answered by saying, ‘Go back from where you came and seek light for yourselves there, for there is no way for you to borrow from Our light.’ And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: On the Day when the hypocrites, men and women, will say… until His statement: And wretched is the destination. Ibn Abbas said: While the people were in darkness, God sent a light. When the believers saw the light, they headed towards it. The light was a guide from God to Paradise. When the hypocrites saw the believers departing, they followed them, so God cast darkness upon the hypocrites. Then they said, Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light, for we were with you in the world. The believers said, Go back from whence you came from the darkness and seek the light there. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, On the Day when the hypocrites, men and women, will say to those who believe, the verse: Ibn Abbas used to say while the people were in darkness, then he mentioned something similar. And His statement, Then He placed between them a wall with a door, inside of which is mercy, but outside of which is torment. God Almighty says, Then God placed between the believers and the hypocrites a wall, which is a barrier between the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, with a wall with a gate, he said, like the veil in Al-A’raf. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, A wall has been placed between them with a gate. The wall is a partition between Heaven and Hell. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And a wall will be placed between them with a gate, he said: This is the wall about which God said, And between them is a veil. It has been said that this wall is in Jerusalem near the Valley of Hell. Who said that? Ali told me: Al-Hasan bin Bilal told us: Hammad told us: Abu Sinan told us: I was with Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas at the Valley of Hell, and he narrated on the authority of his father that he said: A wall will be placed between them with a door, inside of which is mercy, but on the outside of which is torment. He said: This is the location of the wall at the Valley of Hell. Ibrahim bin Atiyah bin Radhih bin Atiyah told me: My uncle Muhammad bin Radhih bin Atiyah told me on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz on the authority of Abu Al-Awam on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit that he used to say: A door whose interior contains mercy and whose exterior contains torment. He said: This is the door of mercy. Ibn Al-Barqi told us: Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Atiyah bin Qais, on the authority of Abu Al-Awam, the muezzin of the Holy House, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-As say: The wall that God mentioned in the Qur’an, and He placed between them a wall with a gate, inside of which is mercy, and outside of which is torment, is the eastern wall, inside of which is the mosque, and outside of which is the valley of Hell. Muhammad bin Awf told me: Abu Al-Mughira told us: Sufyan told us: Shureih told us that Ka’b used to say about the gate in Jerusalem that it is the gate of which God said: And He placed between them a wall with a gate, within it is mercy, but outside it is torment. And His statement, It has a door, its interior contains mercy, God Almighty says: That wall has a door, its interior contains mercy, and its exterior, from the perspective of that exterior, is torment, meaning Hell. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And its apparent meaning is the torment before it, meaning the Fire. Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, Inside it is mercy, he said: Paradise and what is in it.
57:14: And His statement: They will call out to them, ‘Were we not with you?’ They will say, ‘Yes.’ God the Almighty says: The hypocrites will call out to the believers when a wall has been placed between them, so they remain in darkness and torment, while the believers are in Paradise: Were we not with you in the world, praying and fasting, marrying you and inheriting from you? They will say, Yes. He says: The believers will say, Yes, rather you were like that, but you tempted yourselves and became hypocrites. And their temptation in this instance was hypocrisy. And so said the people of interpretation. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you tempt yourselves, he said: Hypocrisy. The hypocrites were with the believers when they were alive, marrying them, cheating on them, and socializing with them, and they were with them when they were dead, and they will all be given the light on the Day of Resurrection, and the light will be extinguished from the hypocrites when they reach the wall, and they will be distinguished from each other at that time. His saying: And you waited means: And you waited in faith and defended yourself by acknowledging God and His Messenger. Some of the interpreters said something similar to what we said about this. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And you waited, he said: By believing in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he recited: Then wait, for we are with you waiting. (al-Baqarah 2:52). Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And you waited means: You waited for the truth and its people. And his statement: And you doubted means: You doubted the oneness of God and the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, and you doubted, that he doubted. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And you doubted they were in doubt about God. His statement: And your desires deceived you means: And your desires deceived you and turned you away from the path of God and led you astray. Until the command of God came means: Until God’s decree came regarding your desires and swept you away. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And wishful thinking deceived you until the command of God came They were deceived by Satan, and by God they continued to be deceived until God threw them into the Fire. His statement, And the Deceiver has deceived you concerning God, means: And Satan has deceived you concerning God, making you hope to escape His punishment and be safe from His torment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The deceiver means the devil. Bishr told us: Zaid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And the Deceiver has deceived you concerning God, meaning Satan. Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And the Deceiver has deceived you concerning God, that is, Satan.
57:15: God Almighty says, informing us of what the believers said to the hypocrites after He distinguished between them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:So today, O hypocrites, no ransom will be taken from you meaning compensation and substitute. He says: That will not be taken from you in exchange for your punishment and torment, thus saving you from the torment of God. Nor from those who disbelieved He says: Nor will ransom be taken from those who disbelieved. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: So today no ransom will be taken from you or from those who disbelieved, meaning the hypocrites and those who disbelieved. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, So today nothing will be taken from you from the hypocrites nor from those who disbelieved with you your refuge is the Fire. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, So today no ransom shall be taken from you. The majority of reciters recited it with the letter ya “yu’khidh,” and Abu Ja’far al-Qari’ recited it with the letter ta. The first of the two readings is correct with the letter yaa, although the other is permissible. His saying: Your abode is the Fire means: Your abode and dwelling place in which you will reside on the Day of Resurrection is the Fire. And his saying: It is your master means: Hell is more deserving of you. And his saying: And what an evil destination means: What an evil destination for those who go to Hell.
57:16: God Almighty says, Has it not been time for those who have believed? Has it not been time for those who have believed in God and His Messenger for their hearts to soften at the remembrance of God, so that their hearts submit to Him and to what has been revealed of the truth, which is this Qur’an that He revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? He said: Their hearts should obey. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? The verse mentioned to us that Shaddad bin Aws used to narrate on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, The first thing that will be lifted from people is humility. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Shaddad ibn Aws used to say: The first thing that will be raised from people is humility. The reciters differed regarding his statement, And what has come down of the truth. The majority of reciters read it as ghair mushbih and nafi’ with the emphasis nazal. And mushbih and nafi’ read it as wa ma nuzal with the emphasis. Whichever of the two readings the reciter reads, he is correct because their meanings are similar. And His statement, And they will not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and a long period passed over them. God Almighty says: Has it not been time for them to be like those who were given the Torah and the Gospel before them? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated from Mughirah from Abu Ma’shar from Ibrahim who said: Atris ibn Arqoub came to Ibn Mas’ud and said: O Abdullah, he is doomed who does not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. Abdullah said: He is doomed who does not recognize good in his heart and forbid what is wrong in his heart. When the time of the Children of Israel became long and their hearts hardened, they invented a book from between their hands and feet. Their hearts were captivated by it and their tongues considered it permissible. They said: We will present this book to the Children of Israel. Whoever follows it, we will leave him, and whoever disbelieves in it, we will kill him. He said: So a man from among them put the Book of God in a horn, then he put the horn between his breasts. When it was said to him: Do you believe in this? He said: I believe in it, and he pointed to the horn between his breasts. Why should I not believe in this book? The best of their religions today is the religion of the owner of the horn. What he means by his saying, A long period passed over them is the period between them and Moses, peace be upon him, and that period is time. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hussein told us: Warqa’ told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the term, he said: time. And His statement: Their hearts have hardened from good deeds and have become inclined to abide by the sins of God, and many of them are wicked. God Almighty says: And many of those who were given the Scripture before the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are wicked.
57:17: God Almighty says: Know, O people, that God gives life to the dead land that produces nothing after its death, meaning after it has been destroyed and eroded. He says: Just as We give life to this dead land after it has been eroded, so too do We guide the person who has strayed from the truth to the truth, so We grant him success and make him steadfast in faith until he becomes a believer after his disbelief and guided after his misguidance. And His statement: We have made clear to you the signs that you may understand. He says: We have made clear to you the evidence and arguments so that you may understand.
57:18: And His statement: Indeed, the men and women who believe The reciters differed in their recitation of that, so most of the reciters of the regions except Ibn Kathir and Asim recited it with a shaddah on the sad and the dal, meaning that the men and women who believe in God, then the ta’ is assimilated into the sad, making it a shaddah on the sad, as it was said: O you who are wrapped up (al-Muzzammil 73:1), meaning the one who is wrapped up. Ibn Kathir and Asim recited Indeed, the men and women who believe in God with a shaddah on the sad and a shaddah on the dal, meaning: Those who believe in God and His Messenger. The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is to say: They are two well-known readings, and the meaning of each of them is correct, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. So the interpretation of the speech, according to reading that with emphasis on the two letters: I mean on the sad and the dal, is that the charitable men and women who give charity from their wealth, and loan God a goodly loan meaning by spending in His cause and in what He has commanded to spend in or in what He has encouraged, it will be multiplied for them and they will have a noble reward meaning: God will multiply for them the loans that they lent Him and will pay them back their reward on the Day of Resurrection and they will have a noble reward. He says: And they will have a reward from God for their truthfulness and their loan to Him, noble, and that is Paradise.
57:19: God Almighty says: And those who acknowledge the Oneness of God and the sending of His Messengers, and believe in the Messengers and believe in what he brought them from their Lord - those are the truthful. His saying: And the martyrs are with their Lord. The people of interpretation differed on that. Some of them said: And the martyrs are with their Lord is separate from what came before it, and the report about those who believed in God and His messengers ends with His saying: The truthful ones. And the truthful ones… They are raised by his saying: They. Then he began the report about the martyrs, and it was said: And the martyrs are with their Lord, for them is their reward and their light. And the martyrs in their saying are raised by his saying: For them is their reward and their light. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, my uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And those who believe in God and His messengers - those are the truthful. He said: This is separate. And the martyrs are with their Lord, for them is their reward and their light. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq: “Those are the truthful and the martyrs in the sight of their Lord. They will have their reward and their light.” He said: It is specifically for the martyrs. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: It is specifically for martyrs. He said: Mahran told us on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha: Those are the truthful ones. Then he resumed speaking and said: And the martyrs are with their Lord. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement, And those who believe in God and His messengers - those are the truthful, this is separate. God called them truthful because they believed in God and believed in His messengers. Then He said, “And the martyrs are with their Lord. They will have their reward and their light,” this is separate. Others said that his statement, and the martyrs, is a description of those who believed in God and His Messengers. They said that the report about those who believed ended with his statement, and the martyrs are with their Lord, then the report about what they have began, and it was said: They have their reward and their light. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated: Shu`bah narrated: Abu Qais informed us that he heard Hudhayl narrating. He said: They mentioned the martyrs, and Abdullah said: A man fights for fame, and a man fights to be seen, and a man fights for the world, and a man fights for reputation, and a man fights for spoils. Shu`bah said: This is its meaning, and a man fights seeking the countenance of God, and a man dies in his bed as a martyr. Abdullah recited this verse: And those who believe in God and His messengers - those are the truthful and the martyrs in the sight of their Lord. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit and Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: “And those who believe in God and His messengers - those are the truthful and the martyrs in the sight of their Lord. They will have their reward and their light.” He said: Every believer is a martyr. Then he recited it. Salih bin Harb Abu Muammar told me: Ismail bin Yahya told us: Ibn Ajlan told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The believers of my nation are martyrs. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: And those who believe in God and His messengers - those are the truthful and the martyrs in the sight of their Lord. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The truthful and the martyrs are with their Lord, he said: By believing in God for themselves. Others said that the witnesses with their Lord in this context are the prophets who testify against their nations, as God Almighty says: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? (An-Nisa’: 41). What I think is most correct of the statements on this matter is the statement of the one who said: The speech and the report about those who believed ended with His saying, Those are the truthful ones, and His saying, And the martyrs are with their Lord, is a predicate of the martyrs. We said that this is the most correct of the sayings about it because this is the most prevalent of its meanings in appearance, and that faith does not require, in the common usage, the name martyr for the believer in any other meaning, unless what is meant by it is a martyr for what he believed in and confirmed, in which case that would be correct, even if there is some distance in it, because that is not among the common usages of its meanings if it is used without a conjunction. So the interpretation of his saying, And the martyrs are with their Lord, for them is their reward and their light, is: And the martyrs who were killed in the way of God or perished in His way are with their Lord, for them is God’s reward for them in the Hereafter and their light. And His statement, And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire. God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve in God and deny His proofs and arguments - those are the companions of Hellfire.
57:20: God the Almighty says: Know, O people, that the enjoyment of worldly life hastened for you is nothing but play and amusement with which you amuse yourself and adornment with which you adorn yourself and boasting to one another about the abundance of its riches and children. And multiplying in wealth and children. God the Almighty says: And some of you boast to one another about the abundance of wealth and children. Like a rain whose growth pleases the disbelievers, then it withers. God the Almighty says: Then that growth dries up, and you see it yellow after it had been green and fresh. And His statement: Then it will be debris, God Almighty says: Then that plant will be debris, meaning that it will be a dry, shattered plant. And in the Hereafter is a severe punishment, God Almighty says: And in the Hereafter is a severe punishment for the disbelievers, “And forgiveness from God and approval” for the people of faith in God and His Messenger. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement verse, he says: People will turn to these two letters in the Hereafter. Some of the Arab scholars, in his statement, And in the Hereafter is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval, mentioned those in this world and that it is as described. As for the Hereafter, it is either punishment or Paradise. He said: The waw in it and the or are in the same position. And His statement: And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion. God Almighty says: And the adornment of the life of this world, hastened for you, O people, is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion. Ali bin Harb Al-Mawsili told us: Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The space of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it.
57:21: God Almighty says: Race one another O people, to do deeds that will bring you “forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth. This Paradise has been prepared for those who believe in God and His Messengers,” meaning those who believed in the Oneness of God and believed in His Messengers. And His statement: That is the bounty of God which He gives to whom He wills, meaning, the Most High is saying: This Paradise, whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, which God has prepared for those who believe in God and His Messenger, is the bounty of God which He has bestowed upon the believers. And God gives His bounty to whom He wills of His creation, and He is the possessor of great bounty upon them, because He has expanded for them provision in this world, bestowed upon them blessings, and made them aware of the place of gratitude. Then He will reward them in the Hereafter for their obedience with what He has described as having prepared for them.
57:22: God Almighty says: No disaster befalls you, O people, on the earth with its barrenness, drought, loss of crops, or corruption, “nor in yourselves with ailments, pains, or diseases, except that it is in a Book meaning except in the Mother of the Book before We bring it into being meaning: before We bring the souls into being, it is said that He brought this thing into being, meaning He created it, so He is its Creator. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into existence, he said: It is something that has been completed before We bring the soul into existence. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Whatever disaster strikes upon the earth: As for the disaster of the earth, it is the years. As for in yourselves, it is these diseases and afflictions. Before We bring them into being: before We create them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: Whatever disaster strikes upon the earth, he said: It is the years, “nor within yourselves,” he said: It is the pains and diseases. He said: It has reached us that no one is afflicted with a prick from a stick, a cut on the foot, or a vein except for a sin, and what is forgiven is greater. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Mansur ibn Abd al-Rahman who said: I was sitting with al-Hasan when a man said: Ask him about the verse, No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being. So I asked him about it and he said: Glory be to God, and who doubts this? Every disaster between the heaven and the earth is in the register of God before a soul is brought into being. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement, No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being, he said: It is something that has been completed and prevented before We bring it into being, before We bring the souls into being. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about the statement of God, the Most High: In a Book before We bring them into being, he said: Before We create them. He said: Calamities, sustenance, and all the things that you like and dislike, God finished all of that before He brought souls into being and created them. Others said: What he meant by that is: what befalls a calamity in religion or the world. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being, meaning: in religion and in this world except that it is in a register before We create it. The Arabists differed about the meaning of fi which comes after his saying except. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He means, and God knows best, except it is in a book, so it is permissible to omit it. He said: He says: I have this, there is nothing except him, he means except him. And someone else among them said: His saying in a book is from the connection of what he hit, and the omission of he is nothing, and he said: His saying I have this, there is nothing except is like it, because except is sufficient from the verb, as if he said: There is nothing other than it. And His saying: Indeed, that is easy for God means that God Almighty says: Indeed, the creation of souls and the enumeration of the calamities that they will encounter is easy and simple for God.
57:23: He, the Most High, means: No calamity befalls you, O people, in your wealth or in your souls, except that it was written in a book before We created your souls, so that you will not despair meaning: so that you will not grieve over what you missed of this world, for you did not attain it, nor rejoice over what He gave you of it. The meaning of his saying with what He has given you if you lengthen the alif is with what your Lord has given you from it, and made you your king and empowered you, and if you shorten the alif then its meaning is with what He has given you from it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us on the authority of Ali on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So that you will not grieve over what has escaped you of this world nor rejoice over what He has given you of it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Tahan, who said: Ishaq bin Mansur narrated to us on the authority of Qais on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So that you will not grieve over what has escaped you. He said: Patience in times of calamity and gratitude in times of blessing. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak Al-Bakri, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So that you will not grieve over what has escaped you. He said: There is no one who does not grieve and rejoice, but whoever is afflicted with a calamity, he turns it into patience, and whoever is afflicted with good, he turns it into gratitude. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of God Almighty, So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you and not rejoice over what He has given you, he said: Do not grieve over what has escaped you of this world and do not rejoice over what He has given you of it. The reciters differed in his saying by what He has given you. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Kufa read it as by what He has given you with a long alif, and some of the reciters of Basra read it as by what He has given you with a short alif. It seems that whoever read it with a short alif chose to read it that way, since what came before it was by what you missed and not by what you missed, so the action is referred back to God, so he attached his saying by what He has given you to it and did not refer it back to it being report from God. The correct thing to say about that is that they are two readings, both of which have a correct meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct, even though I choose to lengthen the alif because of the large number of reciters of that. And the meaning that the weak reciters have used in their criticism of the short alif does not have much meaning, because what is made of that as report from God and what is diverted from it to report from someone else is not outside of it, all of it, according to its listeners from the people of knowledge, is from the action of God Almighty. So what is lost from this world is he who has missed something from it, and what is attained from it is what is attained from the progress of God Almighty and His decree. And He, may His praise be glorified, has made that clear to whoever understands it by His saying, No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being, so He informed that what was lost from it was lost to them by His missing it, and what was attained from it was by His giving it to them, and that it was preserved for them in a register before He created them. And his saying: And God does not love anyone who is arrogant and boastful, meaning: God does not love anyone who is arrogant about what he has been given in this world and boasts about it to people.
57:24: God Almighty says: God does not love any arrogant, boastful misers with what they have been given in this world. They are arrogant and boastful about it to people. They are miserly in giving God’s right that He has made obligatory upon them and they are stingy with it. In addition to their stinginess with it, they also command people to be stingy. And His statement, And whoever turns away, then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, God Almighty says: And whoever turns away, averse to the admonition of God, then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, God Almighty says: And whoever turns away, averse to the admonition of God, abandoning the work to which He has called him of spending in His cause, rejoicing in what he has been given, arrogant therewith, boastful, miserly, then indeed, God is the One free of his own wealth and spending and of all of His creation, the Praiseworthy to His creation for the blessings He has bestowed upon them. The Arab scholars differed about the position of the answer to His statement, Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness on people. Some of them said: It is sufficient to use the report of those like them and for them in the Qur’an, as He said, And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved or the earth could be split asunder or the dead could be made to speak (Ar-Ra’d: 31). There was no report of this position, and God knows best what is revealed, it is as it was revealed or as He intended it to be. Other Arab scholars said: The report has already come in the verse before this, “Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness on people. And whoever turns away - then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.” He connected two parts to one part and made their answer one, as you say, If you stand up and if you do good, I will give you. He did not delete the report. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, For God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy. The majority of the people of Medina read it as, For God is the Rich, without He from the sentence, and likewise in their copies of the Qur’an without He. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as, For God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy, without He in the reading, and likewise in their copies of the Qur’an. The correct thing to say is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
57:25: God Almighty says: We have sent with clear explanations and proofs, and We sent down with them the Book with rulings and laws and the balance with justice. As Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, The Book and the Balance. He said: The Balance is justice. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And We sent down with them the Book and the Balance, with the truth: The Balance is what people do and deal with in this world of their livelihood, which they take and give. They take with a balance and give with a balance that knows what they take and what they give. He said: The Book contains the religion of the people, which they do and leave. So the Book is for the Hereafter and the Balance is for this world. And His statement: So that people may act justly means that God Almighty says: So that people may act justly among themselves. And His statement: And We sent down iron, in which is great force. God Almighty says: And We sent down for them iron, in which is great force. He says: It has great strength. And benefits for the people. This is what they benefit from when they meet the enemy and other benefits from it. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Ahmar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Three things descended with Adam, may God’s prayers be upon him: the anvil, the two bitches, the hammer, and the sword. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And We sent down iron, in which is great force, he said: Great force is the swords and weapons with which people fight, and benefits for people, after they dig with it the earth and mountains and other things. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And We sent down iron, in which is great power and benefits for people, and a shield and a weapon, and He sent it down so that God might know who would support Him. And His statement: And that God may know who supports Him and His messengers in secret, God Almighty says: We sent Our messengers to Our creation and sent down these things with them so that they may be just between them and so that the party of God may know who supports the religion of God and His Messenger in secret from Him. And His saying: Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might. God Almighty says: Indeed, God is Powerful in taking revenge on those who openly display enmity and disobey His commands and prohibitions. He is Exalted in taking revenge on them. No one is able to take revenge on Him from the punishment He has permitted.
57:26: God Almighty says: “And We sent, O mankind, Noah to Our creation and Abraham, his friend, to them as a messenger. And We placed among their descendants prophethood and the Book.” And thus was prophethood among their descendants, and upon them were revealed the books: the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, the Criterion, and all the other well-known books. And among them is he who is guided. He says: Among their descendants is he who is guided to the truth and has insight. And many of them, meaning among their descendants, are wicked, meaning misguided, departing from the obedience of God to His disobedience.
57:27: God Almighty says: Then We followed in their footsteps with Our messengers whom We sent with clear proofs, in the footsteps of Noah and Abraham with Our messengers, and We followed with Jesus, son of Mary. And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him meaning: those who followed Jesus according to his method and law kindness and He is the most merciful and mercy and monasticism, which they innovated meaning: they invented it. We did not prescribe it for them meaning: We did not impose that monasticism upon them except seeking the pleasure of God meaning: but they innovated it seeking the pleasure of God so they did not observe it with its right observance. The interpreters differed regarding those who did not observe monasticism properly. Some of them said: They are the ones who invented it and did not practice it, but they changed and contradicted the religion of God with which Jesus was sent, so they became Christians and Jews. Others said: Rather, they are a people who came after those who invented it, but they did not observe it properly because they were infidels. Rather, they said, We will do as those who were first to do it. So they are the ones whom God described as not observing it properly. In a manner similar to what we said in the interpretation of these letters to the point where we mentioned that the people of interpretation differed in that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told me: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy. These two are from God. Monasticism was invented by a people from among themselves and was not prescribed for them, but they sought thereby and desired the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it as it should be observed. It was mentioned to us that they rejected women and took monasteries. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And monasticism which they innovated. He said: It was not prescribed for them. They innovated it seeking the pleasure of God. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, We did not prescribe it for them, he said, Then why? He said, They innovated it, seeking the pleasure of God voluntarily, but they did not observe it as it should be observed. It was mentioned that those who did not observe monasticism properly were not the ones who invented it, but they were the ones who should be emulated. Al-Husayn ibn al-Harith Abu Ammar narrated: Al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated from Sufyan from Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib from Sa’id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, who said: There were kings after Jesus who changed the Torah and the Gospel, and among them were believers who read the Torah and the Gospel. It was said to their king: We do not find anything more severe for us than the insults that these people insult us with, that they read: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers (al-Ma’idah 5:44). These verses, along with what they criticize us for in their recitation, so call them, let them recite as we recite and believe as we believe in it. He said: So he called them and gathered them and offered them death or to abandon the recitation of the Torah and the Gospel except what they changed from them. They said: What do you want? So leave us. He said: A group of them said: Build us a pillar and raise us to it, then give us something to raise our food and drink with, so that we will not be thrown back to you. A group of them said: Let us wander in the land and wander and drink as wild beasts drink. If you gain control over us in your land, kill us. A group said: Build us houses in the deserts, and we will dig wells and cultivate vegetables, so that we will not come back to you or pass by you. There is no one among them who does not have a close friend among them. He said: So they did that, so God, the Most High, revealed: “And monasticism, which they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its right observance.” The others said: We will worship as so-and-so worships, and we will travel as so-and-so travels, and you will build houses as so-and-so did, and they were in their polytheism, having no knowledge of the faith of those who followed them. He said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent and only a few of them remained, a man descended from his monastery, a traveler came from his travels, and the owner of the house came from his house, and they believed in him and confirmed him. So God, the Most High, said: “O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy.” He said: Two rewards for their belief in Jesus and their belief in the Torah and the Gospel, and their belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their belief in him. He said: And He will make for you a light by which you will walk. The Qur’an and their following the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And peace and blessings be upon him, he said: “So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God and that bounty is in the hand of God. He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.” (al-Hadid 57:29) Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated: Dawud ibn al-Muhbir narrated: al-Sa’aq ibn Hazn narrated: Aqil al-Ja’di narrated: Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani narrated: Suwaid ibn Ghafla narrated: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those who came before us differed into seventy-one sects, three of which were saved and the rest perished. One of the three sects challenged the kings and fought them over the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, so the kings killed them. Another sect did not have the strength to challenge the kings, so they stayed among their people, calling them to the religion of God and the religion of the son of Mary, peace be upon him, so the kings killed them and sawed them through with saws. Another sect did not have the strength to challenge the kings or to stay among their people, calling them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him, so they fled to the wilderness and mountains and became monastics there. This is the saying of God, the Almighty: And monasticism which they invented for themselves, We did not prescribe it for them. He said: They did it only seeking the pleasure of God. “So what…” They took care of it as it should be taken care of.” He said: Those who came after them did not take care of it as it should be taken care of. “So We gave those among them who believed their reward.” He said: They are those who believed in Me and believed Me. He said: And many of them are wicked. He said: They are those who denied Me and called Me a liar. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And monasticism, which they invented for themselves, which we did not write down. Others said that those who worshipped from among the polytheists and those who were destroyed among them say, We worship as so-and-so worships and we wander as so-and-so wanders, while they are in their polytheism and have no knowledge of the faith of those who follow their example. Mention of those who said that those who did not take care of it properly are the ones who invented it. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy to the words the observance of which is due. He says: They did not obey me in it and spoke therein in disobedience to God. This is because God, the Almighty, prescribed fighting for them before He sent Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him. Then when the people of faith were expelled and only a few of them remained and the polytheists increased in number and the messengers were gone and were subjugated, they secluded themselves in caves. This continued with them until a group of them disbelieved and abandoned the command of God, the Almighty, and His religion and took to innovation, Christianity and Judaism, but they did not observe them as they should be observed. A group remained steadfast in the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, when he came to them with clear proofs and God, the Almighty, sent Muhammad as a Messenger, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and they were like that. This is what His statement: “O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy” to And God is Forgiving and Merciful. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd narrated to us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement, And monasticism, which they innovated for themselves, We did not prescribe it for them, God, the Almighty, had prescribed fighting for them before He sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then when the people of faith were expelled and only a few of them remained, and the polytheists increased in number and the messengers were cut off, they isolated themselves from the people and became ghouls. They remained like that until a group of them changed their ways and abandoned the religion of God, His command and His covenant which He had enjoined upon them, and they adopted innovations, so they innovated Christianity and Judaism. Then God, the Almighty, said to them, They did not observe them with their right observance, and a group of them remained steadfast in the religion of Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace, until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they believed in him. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us: Zakariya ibn Abi Maryam told us: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: God has prescribed for you the fasting of Ramadan, but He has not prescribed for you the standing in prayer during it. Rather, standing in prayer is something that you have innovated. A people innovated an innovation that God did not prescribe for them, seeking thereby the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it as it should be observed. So God rebuked them for abandoning it, saying: “And monasticism, which they innovated for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it as it should be observed.” The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: Those whom God described as not observing monasticism as it should be observed are some of the sects that invented it. This is because God, the Most High, informed us that He gave those among them who believed their reward. He said: This indicates that among them were those who observed it as it should be observed. If there were not those among them who were like that, they would not have deserved the reward for which God, the Most High, said: So We gave those among them who believed their reward, unless they were after them. Because if those who are their descendants did not observe it, then it is permissible in the speech of the Arabs to say that the people did not observe it in general, and what is meant by them is the present group. A similar example of this has passed in many places in this book. And His statement, So We gave those among them who believed their reward, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: So We gave those among them who believed in God and His Messengers their reward for seeking God’s pleasure and their belief in Him and His Messenger in the Hereafter, and many of them are people of sin and disobedience to Him and belief in Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: Then We gave those among them who believed their reward. He said: Those who observed that truth.
57:28: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger from among the People of the Two Scriptures, the Torah and the Gospel, fear God by performing His obedience and avoiding His disobedience and believe in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas: O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger, meaning those who believed among the People of the Book. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger, meaning those who believed from among the People of the Book. And His statement, He will give you a double portion of His mercy, means He will give you double the reward for your belief in Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him, and the prophets before Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and then your belief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, when he was sent as a prophet. The root of the word kafl is fortune, and its root is what a rider holds onto, holding him back and protecting him from falling. He says, This kafl protects you from punishment, just as a kafl protects a rider from falling. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Ammar Al-Marwazi told us: Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He will give you a double portion of His mercy. He said: Two rewards for their belief in Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him, and their belief in the Torah and the Gospel, and their belief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and their belief in him. He said: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He will give you a double portion of His mercy. He said: Two rewards: their belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their belief in Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Torah and the Gospel. And on his authority, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Harun bin Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He will give you two portions of His mercy, he said: two rewards.
