Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: He will give you double of His mercy, meaning: double. He said: Mihran told us: Ya`qub told us, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ja`far with seventy horsemen to the Negus to invite him. He came to him and invited him, and the Negus responded to him and believed in him. When he was about to return, some of those who had believed in him from his kingdom, and they were forty men, said: Give us permission to go to this Prophet and greet him and help these people at sea, for we know the sea better than they do. So they came with Ja`far to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had prepared for the Battle of Uhud. When they saw the hardship and difficulty of the Muslims, they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for permission. They said: O Prophet of God, we have wealth and we see the hardship of the Muslims. If you give us permission, we will return, bring our wealth, and help the Muslims with it. So he gave them permission and they returned, brought their wealth, and helped the Muslims with it. Then God revealed about them: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it. (al-Qasas 28:52) And from what We have provided them they spend (al-Qasas 28:54). This was the spending with which they helped the Muslims. When the People of the Book heard from those who did not believe in His saying, They will be given their reward twice over for what they patiently endured (al-Qasas 28:54), they fell down on the Muslims and said, “O group of Muslims, as for he among us who believes in your Book and our Book, he will have his reward twice over, and he who does not believe in your Book will have a reward like your rewards. What is your superiority over us?” Then God revealed, “O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy.” So He made their reward for them and increased them in light and forgiveness. Then He said, lest the People of the Book know and this is how Saeed bin Jubayr read it, lest the People of the Book know that they have no power over anything. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, He will give you double of His mercy, he said: double. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He will give you a double portion of His mercy. He said: The two portions are two rewards for their first faith and for the Book that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: In His statement, O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger, meaning those who believed from among the People of the Book, He will give you a double portion of His mercy, he said: A reward for your belief in the first book and the one brought by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, He will give you a double portion of His mercy, he said: Two rewards, the reward of this world and the reward of the Hereafter. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abu Musa: He will give you double portions of His mercy. He said: The double portions are double the reward in the language of Abyssinia. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: “People will be divided into four categories on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:a man who believed in Jesus and then believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will have two rewards; a man who disbelieved in Jesus and then believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will have one reward; a man who disbelieved in Jesus and then disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he incurred wrath upon wrath; and a man who disbelieved in Jesus from among the polytheists of the Arabs and died in his disbelief before Muhammad, so he incurred wrath.” Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told me: My father told me: I asked Saeed bin Abdul Aziz about the guarantee, how much is it? He said: Three hundred and fifty good deeds, and the two guarantees are seven hundred good deeds. Saeed said: Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him asked one of the Jewish rabbis, how much is the best of what you have doubled for you as a good deed? He said: The guarantee is three hundred and fifty good deeds. Omar praised God for giving us two guarantees, then Saeed mentioned the words of God the Almighty in Surat Al-Hadid, He will give you two guarantees from His mercy. I said to him: The two guarantees on a Friday are like this? He said: Yes. In a similar manner to what we have said about this, the hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is authentic. Who said that? Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Muammar ibn Rashid told us, on the authority of Firas, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three who will be given their reward twice: a man who believed in the first book and the second book; a man who had a mother and educated her and educated her well, then freed her and married her; and a slave who worshipped his Lord well and was sincere to his master.” Yaqub told me: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us: Salih ibn Salih al-Hamdani told me, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Salih bin Salih, who heard Al-Sha’bi narrating on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hakim told me: Ishaq ibn al-Furat told us on the authority of Yahya ibn Ayyub: Yahya ibn Saeed told us: Nafi’ told us that Abdullah ibn Umar said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Your appointed times are like the appointed times of those who came before among the nations, like the time between the afternoon prayer and sunset. Your example and that of the Jews and Christians are like that of a man who hired workers and said: ‘Who will work from morning until midday for one qirat?’ So the Christians worked. Then he said: ‘Who will work from the afternoon prayer until sunset for two qirats?’ So you worked.” Ali bin Sahl told me: Sufyan told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar that he heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The example of this nation, or he said my nation, and the example of the Jews and Christians is like that of a man who said: ‘Who will work for me from morning until noon for one qirat?’ The Jews said: ‘We are the Jews.’ So they worked. He said: ‘Who will work from midday until the afternoon prayer for one qirat?’ The Christians said: ‘We are the Christians.’ So they worked, and you Muslims work from the afternoon prayer until night for two qirats. The Jews and Christians became angry and said: ‘We work more and have less reward.’ He said: ‘Have I wronged you in any of your rewards?’ They said: ‘No.’ He said: ‘Then that is My bounty which I give to whomever I wish.’” Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Al-Layth and Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili that he said: I witnessed the sermon of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of the Farewell Pilgrimage. He said many good and beautiful words, and in it was: “Whoever from among the People of the Two Books becomes Muslim will have a double reward and will have the same as we have and will bear the same as we are. And whoever from among the polytheists becomes Muslim will have the same reward and will have the same as we have and will bear the same as we are.” And His statement, And He will make for you a light by which you will walk, the people of interpretation differed as to what is meant by light in this passage. Some of them said: It means the Qur’an. 696 Who said that? Abu Ammar Al-Marwazi told us: Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And He will make for you a light by which you will walk. He said: The Criterion and their followers, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And He will make for you a light by which you will walk. He said: The Criterion and their followers, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And He will make for you a light by which you will walk. He said: The Qur’an. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed, similarly. Others said: What is meant by light in this place is guidance. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, You walk with it, he said: Guidance. The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: God Almighty promised these people that He would make for them a light by which they would walk, and the Qur’an is with the followers of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a light for whoever believes in them and confirms them, and guidance, because whoever believes in that has been guided. And His saying, And He forgives you, means: And He pardons your sins and conceals them from you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, means: God Almighty says: And God is the possessor of forgiveness and mercy.
57:29: God Almighty says: To the believers in Him and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the People of the Book, your Lord will do this to you so that the People of the Book may know that they are not able to do anything of the bounty of God which He has given you and made you special with, because they thought that God had given them preference over all of creation. So God, may He be glorified and exalted, informed them that He had given the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the bounty and honor that He had not given them, and that the People of the Book envied the believers when the verse was revealed: “O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy and provide for you a light by which you will walk and will forgive you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” So God Almighty said: I did that so that the People of the Book may know that they are not able to do anything of the bounty of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger… the verse. He said, When this verse was revealed, the People of the Book envied the Muslims for it, so God, the Almighty, revealed, “So that the People of the Scripture will not know that they have no power… the verse. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say, ‘Our example and the example of the People of the Two Scriptures before us is that of a man who hired laborers to work until the night for one qirat. When it was noon, they grew tired of his work and grew fed up, so he settled the account with them and paid them according to that amount. Then he hired laborers until the night for two qirats to work for him the rest of his work. It was said to him, What is the matter with these people who work the least and are paid the most? He said, Why do I give to whomever I wish? I hope that we will be the ones with the two qirats. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, Two portions of His mercy. He said: It has reached us that when it was revealed, the People of the Book envied the Muslims, so God revealed, So that the People of the Book will not know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God. Abu Ammar told us, he said: Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So that the People of the Scripture who are eavesdropping will not know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. It was said that lest he know is lest he know. It was mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah, it is lest the People of the Book know that they will not be able, because the Arabs make la a connective in every statement that has at the beginning or end a denial that is not explicit, like his saying in the previous denial that was not explicit, What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you? (al-A’raf 7:12), and his saying, And what makes you perceive that when it comes they will not believe? (al-An’am 6:109), and his saying, And it is forbidden for a city which We have destroyed (Al-Anbiya’: 95)… the verse, and the meaning of that is: We destroyed them. We said about that what the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Abu Harun al-Ghanawi told us: Khattab bin Abdullah said: So that the People of the Book will not know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God. He said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us on the authority of Abu al-Mu’alla, who said: Sa’id ibn Jubayr used to say: So that the People of the Book may not know and His statement, and that bounty is in the hand of God means, the Most High said: And so that they may know that bounty is in the hand of God, not them or anyone else among creation. He gives it to whomever He wills means He gives that bounty to whomever He wills among His creation. That is not for anyone other than Him. And God is the possessor of great bounty means, the Most High said: And God is the possessor of great bounty over His creation.
